proposed_comments.title: Preserve deferred drag-package resources
proposed_comments.body:
**Severity:** `high`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/DataPackageTransfer.cs` (`Copy`, `DelayRenderer`), `CommandItemViewModel.cs` in the same directory, and `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/ExtViews/ListItemsView.xaml.cs` (`Items_DragItemsStarting`) and `Pages/ShellPage.xaml.cs` (`QuickAccessShelfItem_DragStarting`).

**Problem:** `Copy` preserves properties and deferred formats but never transfers the source resource map. Copying an HTML payload's format alone loses its referenced resources.

**Why it matters:** Shelf and list-item drags can advertise valid formats while delivering incomplete HTML/image content to the destination.

**Suggested change:**
1. Add asynchronous resource-map preparation using `GetResourceMapAsync`, copy every returned entry into `destination.ResourceMap`, and retain the existing requested-operation, properties, and deferred-format copying. Log resource-map retrieval failures with the existing logger.
2. Prepare a resource-map task when `CommandItemViewModel` refreshes its data package. Provide a synchronous `TryCopy` that returns false while preparation is incomplete; cancel `Items_DragItemsStarting` in that case rather than delivering an unprepared package.
3. Await the asynchronous copy in the shelf drag-start handler under its drag deferral; complete that deferral in `finally`. In `DelayRenderer`, await `GetDataAsync`, log failures, and complete its data-provider deferral in `finally` on success, failure, or cancellation.

**Verification:** Extend `src/modules/cmdpal/Tests/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.UnitTests/QuickAccessShelfResolverTests.cs` to assert resource-map key/value preservation, rejection of an incomplete preparation task, successful copying after preparation, and preservation of operation/properties/deferred text. Build CmdPal UI and run the view-model tests. Drag resource-backed HTML from both the list and shelf and verify the destination receives the referenced resources.

confidence.rationale: The converged fork added DataPackageResourceMapTask, async resource-map copy, TryCopy gating, and regression tests, and the exact upstream head still drops ResourceMap entries.

proposed_comments.title: Do not force copied shelf payloads to move operations
proposed_comments.body:
**Severity:** `high`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Pages/ShellPage.xaml.cs`, especially `QuickAccessShelfItem_DragStarting`, the reorder/pin/remove drag-over and drop handlers, and `CompleteQuickAccessShelfDrag`.

**Problem:** This assignment unconditionally adds `Move` and broadens external packages to `Copy`; the shelf targets also hard-code `AcceptedOperation = Move`. A bookmark package requesting only `Copy` can therefore negotiate a move with an external destination.

**Why it matters:** Explorer may relocate the bookmarked file instead of copying it, and internal shelf drops can report an operation inconsistent with the source package.

**Suggested change:**
1. For a copied external package, set allowed operations from its requested operation, using `Copy` when that operation is `None`; do not unconditionally OR in `Move` or `Copy`. Keep `Move` for shelf-only items without a package.
2. Compute and retain the shelf's preferred accepted operation from those allowed flags (prefer `Copy`, then `Link`, otherwise the allowed `Move`). Use that value in all reorder, pin, and remove drag-over/drop handlers instead of hard-coded `Move`.
3. Reset the retained operation to `None` in `CompleteQuickAccessShelfDrag`, including cancelled and failed drags. Keep pin/reorder/remove model changes separate from the external storage operation.

**Verification:** Build CmdPal UI. Drag a copy-only file bookmark to Explorer and verify the original remains at its path; exercise link-only payloads and ensure `Move` is never advertised for them. Verify reorder, pin, and remove still work with copied payloads and shelf-only items, and that a cancelled drag cannot leak operation state into the next drag.

confidence.rationale: The current handlers force DataPackageOperation.Move even after copying a source package whose RequestedOperation may be Copy or Link; the fork fix tracks and reuses the preferred operation.

proposed_comments.title: Distinguish persisted pins from items shown in the pinned section
proposed_comments.body:
**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/QuickAccessShelfViewModel.cs` (`BuildItems`), `QuickAccessShelfItem.cs` in the same directory (`CreateOrReuse`, `Matches`, `Equals`, `GetHashCode`), and `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Pages/ShellPage.xaml.cs` (reorder eligibility).

**Problem:** `item.IsPinned` describes the winning visual section, not persisted pin membership. With `RecentCommandsPlacement.BeforePinned`, a persisted pin can appear in the recent section with `IsPinned == false`, so this calculation incorrectly makes it pinnable.

**Why it matters:** The UI offers a pin drop that `TryPinItem` rejects, and reorder eligibility conflates section placement with persisted state.

**Suggested change:**
1. Build a set of `(ProviderId, CommandId)` from the pinned-command snapshot in `BuildItems`. Derive persisted membership independently of the composed section, and use it when calculating `CanPin`.
2. Carry a separate `IsPersistedPinned` value through `QuickAccessShelfItem` construction/reuse, matching, equality, and hashing so changed persisted state cannot reuse a stale item.
3. Use persisted membership for source reorder eligibility in the shelf drag-over/drop handlers. Retain visual `IsPinned` for section-specific removal and pinned-section targets.

**Verification:** Extend `src/modules/cmdpal/Tests/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.UnitTests/QuickAccessShelfResolverTests.cs` with a recent-section item that remains persisted pinned: `IsPinned` false, `IsPersistedPinned` true, and `CanPin` false. Cover reuse when persisted state changes, run the view-model tests, and verify recent-first pin/reorder/removal behavior in CmdPal.

confidence.rationale: The fork fix adds IsPersistedPinned, includes it in reuse/equality, computes it from pinned command IDs, and adds a regression for a recent-section item that remains persisted pinned.

proposed_comments.title: Include local directory bookmarks in storage-item drag data
proposed_comments.body:
**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/ext/Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.Bookmark/Pages/BookmarkListItem.cs` (`ClassifyAsync`, `ApplyClassificationResult`) and `src/modules/cmdpal/ext/Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.Indexer/Helpers/DataPackageHelper.cs` (`CreateDataPackageForPath`).

**Problem:** This filter excludes `CommandKind.Directory` and requires `File.Exists`, so an existing folder receives no local path for its drag package even though the shared helper already resolves directories as `StorageFolder`.

**Why it matters:** Local directory bookmarks cannot provide folder storage-item data when dragged from the shelf.

**Suggested change:**
1. Include `CommandKind.Directory` in the accepted local target kinds and allow `Directory.Exists(classification.Target)` alongside `File.Exists` before retaining the target path. Keep missing and non-local targets excluded.
2. Continue passing the classified path through `ApplyClassificationResult` to the existing shared helper; do not duplicate its folder-resolution logic.
3. Add a directory regression beside the existing local-file test in `src/modules/cmdpal/Tests/Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.Bookmarks.UnitTests/BookmarksCommandProviderTests.cs`: create a temporary directory, initialize its bookmark item, await storage-item data, assert one item with that directory path, and clean up in `finally`.

**Verification:** Run the Bookmarks unit tests and confirm both file and directory packages remain supported. Drag a directory bookmark to a storage-item consumer and verify it receives the folder; missing paths and web bookmarks must not gain a spurious local storage payload.

confidence.rationale: The current condition excludes CommandKind.Directory before DataPackageHelper can use its StorageFolder path; the fork fix and new test cover this exact gap.

proposed_comments.title: Keep the indexer drag helper internal
proposed_comments.body:
**Severity:** `low`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/ext/Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.Indexer/Helpers/DataPackageHelper.cs` (`DataPackageHelper`) and `src/modules/cmdpal/ext/Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.Indexer/Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.Indexer.csproj` (`InternalsVisibleTo`).

**Problem:** Sharing this implementation helper with Bookmarks currently makes the entire helper class public.

**Why it matters:** That exposes a broader API than the one intended cross-extension consumer needs. This is a non-blocking API-surface cleanup, not a runtime blocker.

**Suggested change:**
1. Restore `internal static class DataPackageHelper`.
2. In the indexer project's existing friend-assembly item group, retain its unit-test entry and add `InternalsVisibleTo` for the actual bookmark assembly name, `Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.Bookmarks`. Make both edits together so the bookmark call remains accessible.

**Verification:** Build the indexer and Bookmarks dependency chain, then run the Bookmarks unit tests. Confirm `BookmarkListItem` can still call `CreateDataPackageForPath` without publicly exposing the helper.

confidence.rationale: The fork changed the helper back to internal and added InternalsVisibleTo for the bookmark extension, preserving behavior without widening public surface.
